title: Dualizing complex of a smooth proper morphism
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, that is, a quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] scheme, and let $f:X\to S$ be a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] morphism that is smooth of relative dimension $d$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] for an integer $d\ge0$. Let $f^!$ denote the right adjoint of the derived pushforward $Rf_*$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image] on quasi-coherent complexes. Let $\Omega^1_{X/S}$ be the sheaf of relative Kähler differentials, defined as in [def-sc-kahler-differentials] with $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ replaced by $f$: $\Omega^1_{X/S}:=\Delta^*(\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2)$, where $\Delta:X\to X\times_SX$ [def-pc-base-change] is the diagonal (a closed immersion, $f$ being separated) and $\mathcal I$ is the ideal sheaf of the diagonal; on affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$ it is the sheaf associated with the $A$-module $\Omega_{A/R}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Write $\Omega^d_{X/S}:=\bigwedge^d\Omega^1_{X/S}$ for the $\mathcal O_X$-module whose restriction to each such $U$ is the sheaf associated with the $d$-th exterior power $\bigwedge^d_A\Omega_{A/R}$ [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]. Then there is an isomorphism $f^!\mathcal O_S\cong\Omega^d_{X/S}[d]$ in the derived category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-smooth-proper-dualizing-tensor-evaluation] to the specified R, comparison, a, adj, O and hO. With A=a(O) and N=(wedge^d Hom(Ω¹_{X/S},O_X))[-d], obtain e:A tensor N ≅ 1.

Relative differentials are finite locally free of rank d by [lem-sc-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free]. Apply [lem-sc-shifted-determinant-dual-evaluation] to M=Ω¹_{X/S}. With D=(wedge^d Ω¹_{X/S})[d], obtain v:N tensor D ≅ 1.

Compose the inverse right unitor A ≅ A tensor 1, the tensor of id_A with v inverse, the inverse associator A tensor (N tensor D) ≅ (A tensor N) tensor D, the tensor of e with id_D, and the left unitor 1 tensor D ≅ D. The resulting isomorphism is A ≅ D, exactly the claimed conclusion.
